name: Hawaii

statute.name: Uniform Information Practices Act (Modified) (UIPA)
statute.citation: Haw. Rev. Stat. ch. 92F (access § 92F-11; suit § 92F-15; OIP § 92F-41 et seq.)

response.rule_text: For formal requests the agency has ten business days to disclose records released in full, or to give notice if records will be segregated, Haw. Code R. § 2-71-13; in extenuating circumstances it may acknowledge within ten business days and give written notice within twenty business days.

fees.labor_rule: OIP rules set fees for searching, reviewing and segregating records; reproduction costs may include labor for search and reproduction.
fees.copy_rule: Reasonable costs, not less than five cents per page, Haw. Rev. Stat. § 92-21.
fees.waiver_rule: UIPA directs OIP to adopt rules on waivers of fees when the public interest would be served.

residency.rule_text: No citizenship restriction; 'any person' may request, Haw. Rev. Stat. § 92F-11(b).

appeal.body: Office of Information Practices (OIP); then circuit court
appeal.rule_text: A person denied access may appeal to the OIP under Haw. Code R. ch. 2-73 or sue within two years of the denial (Haw. Rev. Stat. § 92F-15); exhaustion not required.

notes: Appeal type is my classification of OIP (RCFP: OIP 'review and rule on' denials); OIP appeal filing deadline not found (court suit window is 2 years). Silence-is-denial not confirmed. Legislature covered except inchoate/draft working papers (§ 92F-13(5)).
